note: Normative inventory of UX patterns. A pattern is a reusable solution to a recurring interaction problem, composed from Design System components. Prefer extending an entry over inventing a parallel solution.

patterns.name: settings-page
patterns.problem: A tenant-admin screen of named settings, each with a control, that must look the same from page to page and save in sections.
patterns.useWhen: System Settings detail pages (MFA, and any new tenant configuration screen).
patterns.avoidWhen: A catalog of records (Custom Attributes, User Identity Correlation, Entitlement Types) — those use DirectoryListPage and a Drawer. Detail rails use InfoRow, not SettingsRow.

patterns.name: grouped-form
patterns.problem: A long create/edit form in a Drawer or Modal has more than one job, and a flat field stack reads as a list instead of those jobs.
patterns.useWhen: Create/edit overlays whose fields fall into more than one job (authorization flow, credentials, endpoints, request shape).
patterns.avoidWhen: System Settings detail pages — those use Settings page. A single-field drawer does not need groups.
